title: Monomial quotient Tor vanishing for an arbitrary chart at a geometric point
statement:
Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], where $A$ is a commutative ring. Let $P$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid written additively and let $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be the structural map of a chart of this log structure; the chart need not identify $P$ with a characteristic monoid. Let $\bar x$ be any geometric point of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $B_{\bar x}=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and give $B_{\bar x}$ its $R=\mathbf Z[P]$-algebra structure by the composite $z^p\mapsto\alpha(p)\mapsto B_{\bar x}$. Here $\mathbf Z[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}\mathbf Zz^p$ with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$. For every monoid ideal $H\subset P$, meaning $H+P\subset H$ and allowing $H=\varnothing$, put $I=\mathbf Z[H]=\bigoplus_{h\in H}\mathbf Zz^h\subset R$. Then, with Tor as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules],
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_1(R/I,B_{\bar x})=0.$$

source.place: Exposé VIII, proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (Kato 1994, 6.1(ii)); arbitrary-chart reduction through Exposé VI, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 70 and 75. Re-split of the original first proof step.

proof.text: Write $B=B_{\bar x}$ and $L=M_{\bar x}$. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], the etale structure-sheaf stalk is the colimit of rings of sections on pointed etale neighbourhoods. Restricting to affine neighbourhoods is cofinal by [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], so this is precisely the ring $B$ defined in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], compatibly with the chart map. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure], $B$ is strictly henselian local. The chart condition of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $L\cong P\oplus_F B^\times$, where $F=\{p:\alpha(p)\in B^\times\}$ and $\alpha$ now denotes the composite to $B$. Thus the chart germ over $B$ is the original log stalk.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; ILO Expose VI 1.1--1.2, printed p. 69 (log chart stalks).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-chart-face-localization-logification] to the given chart at $\bar x$. It says that $F$ is a face and identifies $Q=P_F/F^{\rm gp}$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$, where $P_F=\{p-f:p\in P,f\in F\}$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $P_F$ is integral fs, its units are $G=F^{\rm gp}$, and $Q$ is sharp fs with finite free group completion.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5, printed pp. 98--99; Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-integral-monoid-free-sharpening-splitting] with its integral monoid $R=P_F$, unit group $U=G$ and sharp quotient $B=Q$ (its letter $B$ here denotes a monoid, not our local ring). The hypotheses hold by Step 2. Obtain a monoid section $s:Q\to P_F$ and $P_F\cong Q\oplus G$. This construction permits torsion in $G$; only $Q^{\rm gp}$ is required to be free.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75, splitting the group sequence and restricting to the sharp monoid.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart], applied to the original log regular $X$ and $\bar x$, choose a chart modeled on $\overline M_{\bar x}$ on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood. Use the identification $Q\cong\overline M_{\bar x}$ of Step 2 to write its germ as $b_M:Q\to L$ with structural map $b:Q\to B$. It induces exactly the characteristic identification specified by the original chart.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70, existence of a chart modeled on the characteristic monoid.

proof.text:
Let $H_x$ be the image of $H$ in $Q$. The map $P\to Q$ is surjective: a class represented by $p-f\in P_F$ equals the class of $p$. Therefore $H_x+Q\subset H_x$, since the sum of images of $h\in H$ and $p\in P$ is the image of $h+p\in H$. The comparison [lem-trf-log-chart-face-tor-comparison] applies to the two chart germs over the strictly henselian local ring $B$, with the section $s$ of Step 3 and the sharp chart $b_M$ of Step 4. It gives
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z[P]}_1(\mathbf Z[P]/\mathbf Z[H],B)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathbf Z[Q]}_1(\mathbf Z[Q]/\mathbf Z[H_x],B),$$
where the right coefficient action is $z^q\mapsto b(q)$. This comparison includes the unit-character twist between the original and chosen sharp charts; their structural maps need not be equal.

source.place: Expose VI 3.7(a), printed p. 75 (unit comparison), and Expose VIII proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110 (monomial Tor).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-kato-tor-independence-chart] to the original $X$, $\bar x$, the sharp characteristic chart on the neighbourhood chosen in Step 4, and the ideal $H_x\subset Q$ from Step 5. It gives vanishing of the right-hand Tor group of Step 5. Its monomial ideal $H_x\mathbf Z[Q]$ equals $\mathbf Z[H_x]$: multiplying a basis element indexed by $H_x$ by one indexed by $Q$ keeps its exponent in $H_x$. Hence the displayed comparison proves the required vanishing for the original chart. Empty and total ideals are included by both cited statements, so no properness or nonemptiness restriction on $H$ was introduced.

source.place: Expose VIII proof of Lemma 3.4.3, printed p. 110, citing Kato 1994 6.1(ii).

proof_origin.place: Expose VI 1.1--1.2, 1.6 and 3.7(a), printed pp. 69--70, 75; Expose VIII proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110. Assembly of existing chart, face and Tor statements.
